A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Quantile Q-Learning work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite appendix renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original QQL benchmark results, component and hyperparameter ablations, training curves, and a synthetic distribution-fitting experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds analyses of learned Bellman residuals on four D4RL datasets, together with training-time measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the QQL objectives in Equations 3–7 are unchanged. The network architecture, temperature clipping, quantile estimation, and value regularization also remain unchanged; the new appendix reasoning does not establish an implemented procedure change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same D4RL tasks, two NeoRL2 tasks, and synthetic experiment. Appendix H analyzes HalfCheetah and Walker2d medium and medium-replay datasets already evaluated in v1, without introducing different task requirements or environments.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 and the MXQL training-curve comparison is unchanged. The newly discussed distributional-RL and IVR/EQL methods are not added as evaluated policy baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix H introduces a supplementary evaluation protocol: analyze 8,192 residuals per dataset, normalize them by learned beta(s), fit normal and logistic distributions, and compare their fit statistics. The existing benchmark and ablation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds a substantive test of the central distributional premise using residuals from trained value functions on four D4RL datasets. This extends assumption checking beyond v1's constructed Gumbel toy example. The original component and hyperparameter ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The new residual analysis explicitly reports Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics, fitted distribution parameters, skewness, and kurtosis. v1 already reported toy-experiment goodness-of-fit p-values. The five-seed D4RL and three-seed NeoRL2 reporting remains unchanged, with no stated increase in training runs.

E6.justification: Figures 5–8 add residual-fit results favoring logistic over normal fits; HalfCheetah-Medium-Replay has KS statistics 0.138125 versus 0.235996. Section 5.2 adds QQL/XQL training times of approximately 4/2.5 hours. Existing benchmark scores and ablation results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–4 are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendices C–E add formal latent-variable assumptions, Lemma 3, Corollary 1, GEM dynamics, DMG constraints and backup equations, and Proposition 5's conservative-bound argument. Appendix E also excludes policy-sampled out-of-distribution values from Assumption 1 and identifies them with Q under the policy. The original propositions and proofs remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: quantile-based temperature estimation, mild-generalization value regularization, stable training, and competitive performance using consistent hyperparameters. Additional supporting material does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of temperature sensitivity, a claimed conservative interpretation of policy-sampled values, and an interpretation of logistic residual fits as more realistic than Gaussian fits. It also acknowledges the 1.6-fold training-time overhead and argues that the stability benefits justify it.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 newly discloses RTX 4070 hardware and training times for one million timesteps. Appendix H documents residual construction, normalization, and fitting. The original implementation details and Table 10 are retained in Appendix G, with unchanged code-source information.

R1.justification: Related-work coverage expands substantially to quantile and distributional RL, including QR-DQN, IQN, non-crossing quantiles, and IEQN. Added IVR/EQL discussion, AWR sensitivity references, and Rust–McFadden background connect QQL to previously undocumented research strands.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 subdivides related work, expands background explanations, adds appendix sections, moves original Appendices C/D to F/G, and updates affiliations, acknowledgments, publication information, and several wording errors.

P2.justification: Figures 5–8 introduce a substantial new set of diagnostic displays combining histograms, fitted densities, cumulative distributions, and statistical summary panels. Existing figures and tables retain their designs and content, with changes to placement, spacing, and publication headers.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful real-task residual diagnostics beyond v1's synthetic check, broader research context, and computational-cost transparency. However, new Appendix C.2.1 omits the omega beta mean term required by the Gumbel convention stated in Appendix B.2. Appendix E also asserts that learned out-of-distribution Q equals the true policy value without establishing that equality. These new weaknesses in the formal justification coexist with empirical and documentation gains, preventing a reliable judgment of the net quality change.
